newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario says small T-bill tender due to bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Ontario says small T-bill tender due to bond issue.

text.p: The Ontario Financing Authority on Thursday said it reduced the size of this week's T-bill tender because the overnight issue of two dual-currency samurai bonds reduced its financing needs for the week.

"We did a 20 billion yen samurai issue overnight in Japan and we're getting close to the end of our borrowing needs for fiscal 1996/97, so we though it would be prudent to reduce the size of the auction today," said an official with the government agency.

The Ontario agency this morning sold C$50 million in three-month T-bills and C$25 million in six-month T-bills in it's weekly T-bill tender. In the two previous auctions is had sold C$100 million in three-month T-bills and C$25 million in six-month T-bills.

Ontario last night set two dual-currency samurai bonds in the Japanese market. One was a 15 billion yen 3.25 percent yen/U.S. dollar reverse issue. The other was a 5 billion yen 3.1 percent yen/Australian dollar reverse issue.
The official said the agency had not yet decided what the size of next week's tender will be.
"For next week's (tender), we'll determine midweek of next week what our requirement is," the official said.
